title: Reprogramming mRNA Processing and mRNA-Binding Proteins by Covalent Protein Modifications
content: mRNA processing diversifies the transcriptomes and plays a pivotal role in fine-tuning mRNA abundance, stability, localization, and cellular activity. Our opinion piece spotlights recent advances in small-molecule modulators of both natural and synthetic origin that covalently modulates a key process underpinning RNA processing, namely mRNA-splicing, with the mechanisms of action involving mRNA-binding proteins (RBPs). We further highlight the latest deployment of interdisciplinary research tools in this arena, in particular, tandem application of REX-technologies and Genetic Code Expansion method, that has enabled the discovery of precision covalent ligand signaling events driven by endogenous reactive metabolites that regulate alternative splicing. Collectively, these advances underscore the potential of covalent modulators to remodel mRNA-splicing for new biotechnology and therapeutic applications.
